walkthrough: Goal (S101: the test crops imported first, so a combination copies a crop): choose the picture of a long colour copy myself, rename a copy or delete it; keep my own pictures in order (see them, say how hard each is to copy, delete one I no longer want, knowing what that leaves); on a session's sheet, undo only what I did on the exercise in front of me; and have a coloured value scale judged by lightness as my eye sees it.

Pictures of my own: on the home, Practice options. Add my picture… first asks how hard it is to copy (Entry, Simple, Medium, Hard, each with what it holds); I tap Entry and the picture picker opens; I choose a picture. The options now show My pictures with how many; tapped, it lists each picture small with its tier and whether it has an outline. Tapping one shows it larger with its tier as four words; I move it to Medium. Its bin asks before it deletes it.

A copy of a picture I choose: New copy… shows a picker: the tiers as words and My pictures, the chosen tier's pictures as rows, each small with its title and its credit; a picture copied before says so. I choose Medium and the vase: the copy begins, the vase beside an empty frame of its shape. I paint a stroke and go back home. The options list 'Colour copy 1' with the vase small beside it and its options button.

Rename and delete: the copy's options button shows its page: the vase larger with its title and credit, Open, Rename… and Delete…. Rename… opens the naming dialog; I type 'Vase study'; the page shows the new name, so does the list. Delete… asks 'Delete “Vase study”?': my painting on it goes for good, its picture stays. Delete: the copy is gone from the list.

Deleting a picture a copy used: I begin a copy of my own picture (New copy…, My pictures; a copy's How told once already) and paint on it. Back in My pictures its bin asks 'Delete “Picture 1”?' and says what that leaves: no session and one colour copy used it; they keep my strokes and where it lay they say 'Picture deleted'. Delete. The copy stays in the list, 'Picture deleted' beside it; opened, its frames are where they were, my stroke is there, the original's frame says 'Picture deleted' and Compare is greyed.

Undo on a lesson's sheet: a lesson of Lines at level 1 from the home. On the first line I draw a line and Compare; Next. On the second line I draw a line and undo it; Undo then does nothing more: the first line's stroke and its Compare stay. Redo brings my line back. Home leaves the lesson under way.

A coloured value scale: a lesson of Value scales at level 1; Next passes its grey scale to its second, a hue. I pick its dark end with the eyedropper, then in the wheel's square move only up for lighter cells, a cell at a time with Fill cell. Compare (S97): the even scale in lightness as the eye sees it, hue held, as a row under mine, cell under cell, each uneven cell outlined red together with its even one, the card its title and '2 cells uneven.' (S97 changed this checkpoint: a scale is five cells for a beginner and its ends are drawn from its seed without the cell count, so its dark end picked and the cells filled from it are other colours). In Chinese the card reads the same.
Not here: renaming or deleting from the canvas; a picture's own title; sorting the picker.
